title.narrative: Reducing illegal trafficking of river turtles in Per by improving compliance with anti-trafficking laws and law enforcement

description.narrative: Perus location makes it a hotspot for wildlife trafficking of many species listed in CITES as threatened with extinction or vulnerable to future extinction. USFWS has supported the proponent in responding to the Peruvian governments requests for assistance to combat wildlife traffic domestically and along its borders. Achievements include: National Strategy to Combat Wildlife Trafficking, and securing important international commitments on illegal wildlife trade in border areas (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador). However, implementing these commitments and enabling responsible agencies to improve enforcement controls to combat wildlife trafficking is a challenge. Law enforcement must focus on controlling wildlife trade at exit points which is challenging due the difficulty of distinguishing illegal and legal trade of certain species and identifying laundered specimens that enter the legal trade chain through forged or fraudulent documents. This project will significantly reduce wildlife trafficking to conserve the Yellow-spotted Amazon river turtle (Podocnemis unifilis, CITES Appendix I) as a real-life pilot to address gaps related to trade and control of species, limited interagency coordination and unclear procedures in granting legal permits to manage and export CITES species, and Peruvian citizens limited information and awareness of the legal and illegal wildlife pet trade.
